The elevator list calls this the SUMMIT, subway and Grand Central Terminal level. Its depth is this app's usual one storey below the street: assumed. Opening and landing construction is illustrative: 0.65 m end plates, 2.5 m opening headroom, guard profiles and door thresholds are not surveyed dimensions. Existing source tiers and equipment endpoints are retained. The outline is the MTA's, with a margin: it is not the walls.

Opening and landing construction is illustrative: 0.65 m end plates, 2.5 m opening headroom, guard profiles and door thresholds are not surveyed dimensions. Depth assumed, the deepest that clears the western mezzanine for the 7 below it, whose depth is official: tracks 1.2 m below the platform and 2.3 m of headroom under them. properties.name: Lobby (entrance lobbies and triangular main concourse)

evidence.note: Layout from the city's 1978 interior landmark report: three entrance lobbies (Lexington Ave, 42nd St, 43rd St) lead into a triangular main concourse; the red-marble information booth faces the Lexington Avenue entrance. The interior is a protected landmark, but its current use was not checked; positions are approximate.

Four elevator halls (1978 report); their positions are assumed. The building publishes no current visitor policy. Travel guides mention weekday lobby hours, but that is not an official source: stepping inside is a scenario. Elevators are for tenants and their visitors and are not modelled.
